s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness with urinary retention and cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Subacute, progressive, symmetric lower extremity weakness
Nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots
key_facts: MRI brain and orbits showed no abnormality
MRI spine showed nodular thickening and enhancement of lumbosacral nerve roots
Diffuse heterogeneous T1- and T2-weighted signal abnormalities within bone marrow
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated white blood cell count
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated red blood cell count

s4.champion: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Leukemia Cutis

raw.champion: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Leukemia Cutis
raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous cutaneous lesions (leukemia cutis), severe flaccid quadriparesis, reduced muscle stretch reflexes, and cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing 98% atypical cells/blasts are highly suggestive of Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Leukemia Cutis, which is a subtype of AML that involves the skin and can cause neurological symptoms due to leukemic infiltration of the nervous system.

rejected.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome with Excess Blasts
rejected.why: While myelodysplastic syndrome can have skin manifestations and neurological symptoms, the presence of 98% atypical cells/blasts in the cerebrospinal fluid and the specific pattern of nerve root involvement on MRI are more consistent with acute leukemia

rejected.label: Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a more indolent course and does not usually cause the severe neurological symptoms or the specific cerebrospinal fluid findings seen in this patient

rejected.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
rejected.why: Myeloproliferative neoplasms are a group of diseases that typically present with an overproduction of blood cells and do not usually cause the acute neurological symptoms or the specific cerebrospinal fluid findings seen in this patient

rejected.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
rejected.why: While AML is a possible diagnosis, the presence of leukemia cutis and the specific pattern of neurological involvement make Acute Myeloid Leukemia with Leukemia Cutis a more specific and accurate diagnosis
